title: Global Run-On Sequencing to Measure Nascent Transcription in C. elegans
author: Quarato, Cecere
materials: The following steps describe the procedure to isolate intact nuclei from worms or embryos. The protocol has been tested with 1,000 to 40,000 worms and 40,000 to 300,000 early embryos.1.Resuspend worms or embryos in 1.5 mL of cold Nuclei extraction buffer (NEB) and transfer to a pre-chilled stainless steel tissue grinder on ice.2.Lyse worms to release nuclei by applying 40 dounce strokes.CRITICAL: take a small aliquot of the lysate (10–20 μL) and check that the worms are lysed using a stereomicroscope. Intact bodies and embryos should be absent. If intact corpses are still present, increase the number of dounce strokes.3.Transfer the lysate to a pre-chilled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.Note: Multiple samples can be processed simultaneously. If so, keep lysate from step 3 on ice while lysing the other samples. In this case, wash the metal dounce well between each sample with milliQ water. After processing all the samples, proceed immediately to step 4.4.Remove debris by centrifuging at 100×g for 4 min at 4°C.5.Transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 mL low binding microcentrifuge tube.CRITICAL: carefully collect the supernatant without disturbing the debris pellet. If necessary, repeat steps 4 and 5 until lysate is clear from debris. A residual 50–100 μL can be left in the tube to avoid debris carryover.6.Pellet nuclei by centrifuging at 1,000×g for 4 min at 4°C.7.Remove supernatant and wash nuclei with 1 mL NEB.CRITICAL: wash nuclei by pipetting up and down several times using a wide-bore tip. Gently pipette nuclei to preserve their integrity.8.Pellet nuclei by centrifuging at 1,000×g for 4 min at 4°C.9.Repeat steps 7 and 8 three more times for a total of 4 washes with NEB.10.Wash nuclei in 1 mL Freezing buffer NO-Glycerol.CRITICAL: wash nuclei by pipetting up and down several times using a wide-bore tip. Gently pipette nuclei to preserve their integrity.11.Pellet nuclei by centrifuging at 1,000×g for 4 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.12.Resuspend nuclei in 100 μL Freezing buffer.Pause point: nuclei in the Freezing buffer can be stored at −80°C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Isolate nuclei from worms/embryos
steps.instruction: Perform all steps on ice (4 °C) using nuclease‑free reagents.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend 1 000–40 000 worms or 40 000–300 000 embryos in 1.5 mL cold Nuclei Extraction Buffer (NEB) and transfer to a pre‑chilled stainless‑steel tissue grinder on ice.
Lyse by applying 40 dounce strokes; check 10–20 µL aliquot under a stereomicroscope and repeat strokes if intact bodies remain.
Transfer the lysate to a pre‑chilled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube; keep on ice while processing other samples, washing the dounce with milliQ water between samples.
Centrifuge at 100 ×g for 4 min at 4 °C to pellet debris.
Transfer the supernatant to a new low‑binding 1.5 mL tube, being careful not to disturb the pellet; repeat debris spin if necessary, leaving 50–100 µL residual volume.
Pellet nuclei by centrifuging at 1 000 ×g for 4 min at 4 °C.
Wash nuclei with 1 mL NEB by pipetting up/down with a wide‑bore tip; centrifuge again at 1 000 ×g for 4 min at 4 °C.
Repeat the NEB wash (pipette up/down, centrifuge) three more times for a total of four washes.
Wash nuclei in 1 mL Freezing Buffer NO‑Glycerol (same pipetting method).
Pellet nuclei at 1 000 ×g for 4 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the washed nuclei in 100 µL Freezing Buffer.
Pause point: nuclei can be stored at –80 °C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Extract total RNA with TRIzol
steps.instruction: Isolate total RNA, including biotinylated nascent RNA, using TRIzol and BCP.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL 1‑Bromo‑3‑chloropropane (BCP) to the TRIzol lysate and vortex thoroughly.
Incubate at room temperature (RT) for 15 min.
Centrifuge at 12 000 ×g for 15 min at 4 °C; carefully transfer ~450 µL of the upper aqueous phase to a new low‑binding tube, avoiding interphase.
Add 2 µL GlycoBlue and vortex 5–10 s.
Add 500 µL isopropanol and vortex vigorously 10–15 s.
Incubate at RT for 15 min to precipitate RNA.
Centrifuge at 12 000 ×g for 15 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant.
Wash the RNA pellet with 1 mL 75 % ethanol; centrifuge at 7 500 ×g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Remove supernatant without disturbing the blue pellet; air‑dry 1–2 min using a p1000 to remove residual ethanol (see detailed removal procedure).
Do not over‑dry the pellet.

steps.title: Prepare streptavidin Dynabeads
steps.instruction: Wash and equilibrate MyOne Streptavidin C1 beads for RNA capture (room temperature 20‑25 °C).

substeps.instruction: Vortex the Dynabeads vial >30 s (or tilt/rotate 5 min) to resuspend.
Transfer 30 µL beads per sample to a low‑binding tube (scale volume if sample size differs).
Add 1 mL Binding & Washing Buffer (1×) and resuspend by pipetting or gentle vortex 5–10 s; briefly centrifuge.
Place on a magnetic stand for 1 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend beads in the original bead volume of Binding & Washing Buffer (1×); repeat magnetic separation and discard supernatant. Perform this wash three times total.
Wash beads twice in Solution A for 2 min (volume ≥ initial bead volume).
Wash beads once in Solution B (same volume as Solution A).
Resuspend the washed beads in 60 µL per sample of 2× Binding & Washing Buffer. Store at 4 °C for up to 1 day if needed.

steps.title: Purify RNA via phenol‑chloroform
steps.instruction: Extract RNA from the TRIzol aqueous phase using Phase‑Lock Gel tubes and precipitate.

substeps.instruction: Spin a “5‑PRIME Phase Lock Gel – Heavy” tube for 2 min at 12 000 ×g at RT (20‑25 °C) to pellet the gel.
Transfer the aqueous phase from the previous step into the pre‑spun Phase Lock tube.
Add 300 µL (1 volume) Phenol/Chloroform/Isoamyl Alcohol; invert 10–15 times (do not vortex).
Centrifuge at 12 000 ×g for 5 min at RT; transfer the upper aqueous phase to a fresh low‑binding tube.
Add 30 µL 3 M sodium acetate and 2 µL GlycoBlue; vortex 5–10 s.
Add 900 µL ethanol; vortex vigorously 10–15 s.
Incubate 1 h at –20 °C (can be overnight).
Centrifuge at 12 000 ×g for 30 min at 4 °C to pellet RNA.
Wash pellet with 1 mL 75 % ethanol; centrifuge 12 000 ×g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Air‑dry the pellet 1–2 min (avoid over‑drying).
Resuspend RNA in 5 µL RNase‑free water.

steps.title: Purify RNA with RNAClean XP beads
steps.instruction: Clean up RNA from the ligation reaction using SPRI beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 60 µL isopropanol (3 volumes) to the ligation reaction.
Add 36 µL Agencourt RNAClean XP beads (1.8 volumes); mix well (beads are viscous).
Incubate 20 min on ice (during this time you may start washing Dynabeads).
Place tube on a magnetic rack for 5 min; carefully remove and discard the cleared supernatant.
Wash beads twice with 200 µL 75 % ethanol (30 s incubation each), removing ethanol each time.
Briefly spin to collect residual ethanol, remove it, and air‑dry beads 5 min (avoid over‑drying).
Elute RNA by adding 61 µL RNase‑free water, pipette to resuspend, incubate 30 s.
Place on magnetic rack 1 min; transfer 60 µL eluate to a fresh tube (1 µL excess water added to prevent bead carry‑over).
Pause point: RNA can be stored at –80 °C for up to 1 week.

steps.title: Purify PCR product with AMPure XP beads
steps.instruction: Remove salts, primers, and dimers from the library PCR using SPRI beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 90 µL AMPure XP beads to 50 µL PCR reaction (1.8 volumes).
Mix by pipetting ≥15 times or gentle vortex; incubate 5 min at RT.
Briefly spin and place on magnetic rack for 5 min; discard supernatant.
Wash beads twice with 200 µL 75 % ethanol (30 s each), removing ethanol each time.
Spin briefly to collect residual ethanol, remove it, and air‑dry beads 5 min (avoid over‑drying).
Elute DNA by adding 18 µL RNase‑free water, pipette to resuspend, incubate 30 s.
Place on magnetic rack 1 min; transfer 17 µL eluate to a fresh tube (add 1 µL excess water to prevent bead carry‑over).

steps.title: Analyze sequencing data
steps.instruction: Process raw GRO‑seq reads to generate expression tables and visualizations.

substeps.instruction: Demultiplex BCL files with bcl2fastq to obtain fastq.gz files (concatenate lanes if desired).
Trim adapters using cutadapt (adapter: TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG) and remove random tetramers from both ends; keep reads ≥24 bp after trimming (≥16 bp after tetramer removal).
Map trimmed reads to the C. elegans genome with bowtie2.
Count features with featureCounts (or equivalent) to produce a count matrix for desired feature classes.
Compute TPM or run DESeq2 for differential expression analysis.
Optionally generate normalized bigWig files (samtools sort/index + deeptools bamCoverage) for IGV visualization.

description: GRO-seq is a powerful technique to map RNA polymerase transcription at the genome-wide level. The assay has been initially developed for human cells (Core et al., 2008) and has been updated and adapted to work in fission yeasts, Drosophila melanogaster, and plant cells (Mahat et al., 2016). Here we describe the specific steps for producing GRO-seq libraries from Caenorhabditis elegans worms and embryos. We have used this protocol to generate GRO-seq libraries from as low as 1,000 worms or 40,000 embryos (Barucci et al., 2020; Quarato et al., 2021; Singh et al., 2021). The protocol can be divided into three main steps:1.Nuclei isolation and nuclear run-on with biotinylated-UTP2.Enrichment of biotin-labeled nascent RNAs and library preparation3.Library amplification and sequencing CRITICAL: all steps of the protocol are performed at 4°C unless stated differently. Pre-chill all reagents and equipment before use. Nuclease-free reagents need to be used in all steps of the protocol.
